channel.title: FXStreet Forex & Commodities News
channel.description: Real-time Forex News and the latest trading updates. Stay updated on the latest news about currencies and commodities markets.

item.title: BoC expected to keep interest rate unchanged as prices stay elevated and growth slows
item.description: The Bank of Canada (BoC) is widely expected to keep its policy rate unchanged at 2.25% on Wednesday. This would be the fifth consecutive gathering with the bank keeping its hand steady.

item.title: Bank of Canada: Policy hold risks highlighted – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Strategist Michael Every expects the Bank of Canada (BoC) to keep its policy rate at 2.25%, in line with Bloomberg consensus and market pricing.

item.title: US Dollar: AI-driven inflows support Dollar – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Volkmar Baur argues that a major US technology IPO could generate sizeable foreign capital inflows, supporting the US Dollar, particularly against the Euro.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Downside against US Dollar eyed as BoC holds – BBH
item.description: Brown Brothers Harriman’s Elias Haddad highlights that USD/CAD has pulled back after testing a six‑month high but still risks grinding higher toward 1.4140.

item.title: Japanese Yen: CPI risks dominate against US Dollar – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lee Hardman and Abdul-Ahad Lockhart note that recent US Dollar (USD) resilience and higher US yields have created a tougher backdrop for FX carry trades, while commodity-linked currencies lag.

item.title: US CPI data expected to show inflation hit a three-year high, driven by high Oil prices
item.description: The US Bureau of Labor Statistics (BLS) will publish the May Consumer Price Index (CPI) data on Wednesday.

item.title: Indian Rupee gains despite renewed Middle East conflicts, US CPI eyed
item.description: The Indian Rupee (INR) rises against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday after a flat opening. The USD/INR pair falls to near 95.15 even as Middle East tensions have flared up again, following the United States (US) retaliation against Iran over the shooting down of an American helicopter.

item.title: Experts agree: RBA’s next move will likely be an interest-rate cut, not a hike
item.description: The Australian Dollar (AUD) underperforms its major currency pairs during the European trading session on Wednesday, trading 0.25% lower to near 0.7010 against the US Dollar (USD).

item.title: Australian Dollar: 0.7000 support under pressure against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann report that AUD/USD spiked to 0.7071 before sliding to 0.7005 and closing at 0.7027. They see slightly stronger downside momentum but doubt a sustained break below 0.7000 in the very near term.

item.title: US Dollar: Core CPI focus keeps DXY supported – ING
item.description: ING’s Chris Turner notes the Dollar is holding recent gains as markets await the US May CPI report, with expectations that firm core inflation will keep Federal Reserve hike pricing alive into December.

item.title: USD/CAD Price Forecast: Could rebound toward six-month highs near 1.4000
item.description: USD/CAD loses ground for the second consecutive day, trading around 1.3930 during the European hours on Wednesday. However, the technical analysis of the daily chart indicates the pair is moving upwards within the ascending channel pattern, signaling an ongoing bullish bias.

item.title: Gold languishes near March low, below $4,200 as traders await US CPI report
item.description: Gold (XAU/USD) maintains its heavily offered tone through the first half of the European session and currently trades near its lowest level since March 23, around the $4,180-$4,175 region.

item.title: Euro: Gains hinge on domestic demand – BNY
item.description: BNY’s Geoff Yu notes that recent EUR/USD support has come mainly from cross-border investors reducing hedges after the European Central Bank's (ECB) hawkish shift, bringing aggregate Euro holdings back to flat.

item.title: Iran blames US for harming diplomatic process with continued ceasefire violations
item.description: Iran's Foreign Ministry spokesperson Esmaeil Baghaei said during the European trading session on Wednesday that Tehran needs to re-assess the terms of negotiations with Washington following overnight clashes, SNN reported.

item.title: British Pound refreshes weekly high vs broadly weaker JPY amid Mideast tensions
item.description: The GBP/JPY cross turns positive for the third straight day following an intraday dip to the 214.30-214.25 region and touches a fresh weekly high during the first half of the European session on Wednesday.

item.title: Canadian Dollar: Downside risks versus USD with BoC on hold – Societe Generale
item.description: Societe Generale analysts note USD/CAD has broken key technical resistance and could extend higher as the Bank of Canada (BoC) is expected to keep rates unchanged at 2.25%.

item.title: Experts agree: Canadian Dollar’s downside pressure may be about to ease
item.description: The Canadian Dollar (CAD) is hovering near the upper boundaries of its year-to-date range against the US Dollar, underperforming as one of the weakest major currencies in recent weeks.

item.title: Dow Jones futures decline ahead of US inflation data
item.description: Dow Jones futures lose 0.30%, trading near 50,750 during the European hours on Wednesday, ahead of the US regular opening. However, S&P 500 futures fall 0.40% to near 7,360, and Nasdaq 100 futures decline 0.61%, trading near 28,950 at the time of writing.

item.title: Hungarian Forint: Softer CPI opens door to rate cuts – Commerzbank
item.description: Commerzbank’s Tatha Ghose highlights that Hungarian inflation has fallen below the lower bound of the MNB’s tolerance range, with underlying measures remaining within target.

item.title: US Dollar Index Price Forecast: Faces selling pressure ahead of US CPI data
item.description: The US Dollar (USD) is under pressure against its major currency peers during the European trading session on Wednesday. As of writing, the US Dollar Index (DXY), which tracks the Greenback’s value against six major currencies, is down 0.1% to near 99.90.

item.title: British Pound: Further downside risk toward 1.3240 against US Dollar – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann note GBP/USD remains under pressure after last week’s plunge, with scope for another test of 1.3300 before a recovery.

item.title: Copper: Mixed China signals and positioning shifts – ING
item.description: ING’s Warren Patterson and Ewa Manthey say China’s latest trade data for Copper are mixed, with higher unwrought Copper imports in May but lower year-to-date volumes due to stronger domestic refined output.

item.title: Euro remains near two-month lows with all eyes on US CPI release
item.description: The Euro (EUR) ticks up for the third consecutive day against the US Dollar (USD) on Wednesday, but remains capped below a previous support zone at 1.1575, with the two-month lows, in the 1.1500 area, at hand.

item.title: S&P 500: Tech-led swings as AI exuberance cools – Deutsche Bank
item.description: Deutsche Bank’s Jim Reid describes a volatile session for US equities, with a sharp intraday tech sell-off largely reversing by the close. The S&P 500 and NASDAQ finished modestly lower, while semiconductors underperformed.

item.title: Oil: Hormuz risks and hidden flows – Rabobank
item.description: Rabobank’s Global Strategist Michael Every highlights that Oil prices fell as the United States (US) energy secretary reported rising Hormuz transits, with evidence the US Navy may be moving more crude through the Strait than official data show.

item.title: US Dollar Index: CPI and geopolitics underpin strength – MUFG
item.description: MUFG’s Lloyd Chan highlights that a potentially hotter US CPI print could reinforce expectations of higher-for-longer US interest rates, underpinning broad US Dollar strength.

item.title: Euro flatlines against British Pound as traders brace for ECB rate decision
item.description: The EUR/GBP cross trades on a flat note near 0.8625 during the early European trading hours on Wednesday. Traders prefer to wait on the sidelines ahead of the European Central Bank (ECB) interest rate decision on Thursday.

item.title: Forex Today: Markets await US inflation data, BoC rate decision
item.description: Here is what you need to know on Wednesday, June 10:

item.title: Euro strengthens against Japanese Yen due to ECB rate hike odds
item.description: EUR/JPY extends its gains for the third successive day, trading around 185.30 during the early European hours on Wednesday.

item.title: Japanese Yen: Weakens gradually against US Dollar toward 160.75 – UOB
item.description: UOB’s Quek Ser Leang and Lee Sue Ann describe USD/JPY as range-bound intraday between 159.90 and 160.40 after a brief spike and reversal, but maintain a slightly positive multi-day stance.
